# Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It

Day 3, 13:55 · Ariel Kroszynski, Front-End Engineering Manager, Search Console · coverage: transcript, slides

Named on the title slide. Query groups, AI-powered report configuration, AI reporting, social platform properties and multimodal search reporting.

## Claims

- **[Stage]** Google's Search Console talk at the Deep Dive covered five Search Console launches of the past year: query groups, AI-powered configuration of the Performance report, generative AI control and reporting, platform properties for social accounts, and multimodal search reporting.
  <br><sub>`D3-C412` · Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It (Ariel Kroszynski)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Search Console's query groups put together queries that express a very similar user intent but are written differently, for example with more or fewer words or with spelling errors, so site owners can see the intent behind their traffic instead of every query string.
  <br><sub>`D3-C413` · Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It (Ariel Kroszynski) · confirmed by Google docs · [Introducing Query groups in Search Console Insights](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2025/10/search-console-query-groups) · Used by the glossary term *Query groups*</sub>

- **[Slide]** To show how diverse queries for one intent are, Google's Search Console talk showed a slide titled 'How to spell Britney Spears?' with a long list of spelling variants, citing archive.google/jobs/britney.html.
  > "How to spell Britney Spears?"
  <br><sub>`D3-C414` · Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It (Ariel Kroszynski) · confirmed by Google docs · [Britney Spears spelling correction](https://archive.google/jobs/britney.html)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google's Search Console talk said Google's logs show hundreds of different ways in which people write the query for Britney Spears.
  <br><sub>`D3-C415` · Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It (Ariel Kroszynski) · consistent with Google docs · [Britney Spears spelling correction](https://archive.google/jobs/britney.html)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** The Google archive page cited on the Britney Spears slide lists 593 spellings (the correct one plus 592 misspellings), each typed by at least two different users within a three-month period and corrected by Google's spelling system; it is an old jobs page (footer 2011), so the figures are historical.
  <br><sub>`D3-C416` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google said query groups are not built by matching query text alone: deciding which queries belong in which group goes beyond simple text filtering.
  <br><sub>`D3-C417` · Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It (Ariel Kroszynski) · consistent with Google docs · [Introducing Query groups in Search Console Insights](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2025/10/search-console-query-groups) · Extended by [D3-C473](D3-S13-lightning-session-l-understanding-serps-and-your-users.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google named granularity as a design challenge of query groups: putting many queries into one large group versus splitting them into smaller, more specific groups.
  <br><sub>`D3-C418` · Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It (Ariel Kroszynski) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Stage]** Query groups can change when the meaning of a query changes over time: a 2023 search for 'Gemini' may have meant the astrological sign, but after Google launched Gemini it means something else, so Search Console may now group it differently.
  <br><sub>`D3-C419` · Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It (Ariel Kroszynski) · consistent with Google docs · [Introducing Query groups in Search Console Insights](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2025/10/search-console-query-groups)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google acknowledged that query grouping is not perfect: some queries are not understood, and some are not grouped in a logical way.
  <br><sub>`D3-C420` · Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It (Ariel Kroszynski) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Stage]** Query groups appear in the Search Console Insights report as a table of the top groups, showing the total clicks of all the queries inside each group, with an option to view a larger table.
  <br><sub>`D3-C421` · Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It (Ariel Kroszynski) · consistent with Google docs · [Introducing Query groups in Search Console Insights](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2025/10/search-console-query-groups)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** For content planning, read query groups (and their trending up and trending down views) as intent themes: write for the intent the group stands for, not for each spelling or phrasing variant in it.
